name: reward
title: Reward
description: One thing a player can be given: a prize, a badge, a pack, a ticket. Four lifecycle states on `data-gs-reward-state`, locked, available, earned and claimed, each changing the surface, the glyph and the text at once rather than the colour alone. The lifecycle is deliberately not `data-gs-state`, which is set once after settlement and never revisited; a reward is host-driven and comes back. An earned reward that has not been opened pulses, and because the pulse is motion and stops dead under reduced motion, waiting is also a glyph, a fill, and the word "waiting" in the accessible name. Revealing is a player act, so a revealable reward is a real button that works from the keyboard. Performs nothing: it does not decide a reward was earned, fetch it or claim it.
docs: Pass `state` for where the reward is in its lifecycle; the host owns it and changes it, the component never does. Pass `revealed` once the reveal has played: an earned reward without it is waiting, and it says so. Pass `onReveal` to let the player open it, which makes the root a real button, focusable and operable with Enter and Space; leave it off and the reward is an object to look at. `value` renders beside the name and rides `data-gs-value` machine-readably. A locked reward carries `data-gs-reward-state="locked"` and never `data-gs-locked`, which stays a control attribute. Installs into components/gamestage/reward/ rather than a flat file, because `inventory` imports it by a path that has to resolve the same here and in your app.
